summary.en: The sisters Trưng Trắc and Trưng Nhị led the Lạc lords of the Red River delta in revolt against the Han governor of Jiaozhi and ruled for about three years from Mê Linh, until the Han general Ma Yuan crushed the rising in 43.
summary.zh: 征侧、征贰姐妹率领红河三角洲的雒将起兵反抗东汉交趾太守，以麊泠为中心自立约三年，43年被东汉将领马援镇压。

sources.title: Hou Hanshu (Book of the Later Han), "Biography of Ma Yuan" and "Treatise on the Southern Man"
Keith W. Taylor, The Birth of Vietnam (University of California Press, 1983)
Đại Việt sử ký toàn thư (Complete Annals of Đại Việt, 1479; 1697 ed.)
Wikipedia: Trưng sisters' rebellion

name.en: Kedukan Bukit inscription: rise of Srivijaya
name.zh: 格杜干武吉碑：室利佛逝兴起

summary.en: This Old Malay inscription found at Palembang records a sacred expedition by Dapunta Hyang with an army of some 20,000 in 683, commonly read as the founding of the Srivijaya polity that soon dominated the Strait of Malacca.
summary.zh: 在巨港发现的这块古马来语碑铭，记载了683年达本达·希扬率两万大军进行的神圣远征，通常被解读为室利佛逝政权的建立；此后不久它便称霸马六甲海峡。

sources.title: George Cœdès, The Indianized States of Southeast Asia (University of Hawaii Press, 1968)
O. W. Wolters, Early Indonesian Commerce: A Study of the Origins of Śrīvijaya (Cornell University Press, 1967)
Wikipedia: Kedukan Bukit inscription

note: Interpretation of the expedition as a "founding" is debated; the inscription is dated Śaka 605 (683 CE).

summary.en: The Shailendra dynasty of central Java raised Borobudur, the world's largest Buddhist monument: a stepped mandala of nine platforms with over 2,600 relief panels and 504 Buddha statues, built around 780–830.
summary.zh: 中爪哇的夏连特拉王朝建造了世界上最大的佛教建筑婆罗浮屠：一座九层阶梯式曼荼罗，拥有两千六百多块浮雕和五百零四尊佛像，约建于780至830年间。

sources.title: Encyclopaedia Britannica: Borobudur
UNESCO World Heritage Centre: Borobudur Temple Compounds
George Cœdès, The Indianized States of Southeast Asia (University of Hawaii Press, 1968)
Wikipedia: Borobudur

note: No foundation inscription survives; construction is dated by style and epigraphy to c. 780–830.

summary.en: The Shivagrha inscription of 856 records the completion of a great Shiva temple, identified with Prambanan, by the Sanjaya-line ruler of Mataram. Its soaring towers to Shiva, Vishnu and Brahma are Java's largest Hindu monument.
summary.zh: 856年的湿婆屋碑铭记载了马打兰古国桑贾亚系君主建成一座宏伟的湿婆神庙，即普兰巴南。其供奉湿婆、毗湿奴与梵天的高塔是爪哇最大的印度教建筑群。

sources.title: Encyclopaedia Britannica: Prambanan
UNESCO World Heritage Centre: Prambanan Temple Compounds
George Cœdès, The Indianized States of Southeast Asia (University of Hawaii Press, 1968)
Wikipedia: Prambanan

note: Wikidata gives c. 850; 856 is the date of the Shivagrha inscription usually associated with the complex.

summary.en: Ngô Quyền planted iron-tipped stakes in the bed of the Bạch Đằng River and lured a Southern Han fleet over them at high tide; as the tide fell the ships were impaled and destroyed. The victory ended a millennium of Chinese rule in northern Vietnam.
summary.zh: 吴权在白藤江河床中埋下包铁木桩，趁涨潮引诱南汉舰队驶入，退潮时敌船触桩搁浅而被歼灭。此役结束了中国对越南北部近千年的统治。

sources.title: Đại Việt sử ký toàn thư (Complete Annals of Đại Việt, 1479; 1697 ed.)
Keith W. Taylor, The Birth of Vietnam (University of California Press, 1983)
Wikipedia: Battle of Bạch Đằng (938)

name.en: Lý Thái Tổ moves the capital to Thăng Long

summary.en: In his Edict on the Transfer of the Capital, Lý Thái Tổ moved the court from Hoa Lư to the site of the old Tang citadel of Đại La, renaming it Thăng Long ("Ascending Dragon"), the future Hanoi.
summary.zh: 李太祖颁布《迁都诏》，将朝廷从华闾迁至唐代大罗城旧址，并改名升龙（意为“腾飞之龙”），即后来的河内。

sources.title: Đại Việt sử ký toàn thư (Complete Annals of Đại Việt, 1479; 1697 ed.)
UNESCO World Heritage Centre: Central Sector of the Imperial Citadel of Thang Long – Hanoi
Wikipedia: Edict on the Transfer of the Capital

summary.en: King Suryavarman II built Angkor Wat as a temple to Vishnu and probably his own funerary monument. Its five lotus towers, moat and kilometre-long bas-reliefs make it the largest religious monument in the world.
summary.zh: 苏利耶跋摩二世修建吴哥窟，供奉毗湿奴，很可能也是其陵庙。五座莲花状宝塔、护城河与绵延近一公里的浮雕回廊，使其成为世界上最大的宗教建筑。

sources.title: Encyclopaedia Britannica: Angkor Wat
UNESCO World Heritage Centre: Angkor
George Cœdès, The Indianized States of Southeast Asia (University of Hawaii Press, 1968)
Wikipedia: Angkor Wat

note: Wikidata gives an inception of 1200; scholarly consensus places construction in the reign of Suryavarman II (1113–c. 1150).

summary.en: At the centre of his new walled city of Angkor Thom, Jayavarman VII raised the Buddhist Bayon, famous for its towers carved with serene giant faces and reliefs of daily life and wars with Champa.
summary.zh: 阇耶跋摩七世在新建的吴哥城中心修建佛教寺庙巴戎寺，以刻有巨大安详面孔的佛塔群和描绘日常生活及与占婆战争的浮雕而闻名。

sources.title: Encyclopaedia Britannica: the Bayon
UNESCO World Heritage Centre: Angkor
George Cœdès, The Indianized States of Southeast Asia (University of Hawaii Press, 1968)
Wikipedia: Bayon

note: Built over several phases in the late 12th and early 13th centuries; 1190 is an approximate date.

name.en: Mongol invasions of Đại Việt and Champa

summary.en: Three Mongol–Yuan invasions (1258, 1285, 1287–88) took Thăng Long but were each driven out by the Trần dynasty under Trần Hưng Đạo, who used scorched-earth tactics and guerrilla warfare before the decisive river battle at Bạch Đằng.
summary.zh: 蒙古—元朝先后三次（1258年、1285年、1287—1288年）入侵，虽曾攻占升龙，但都被陈朝击退。陈兴道采取坚壁清野与游击战术，最终在白藤江决战中获胜。

label.zh: 兀良合台自大理（云南）出兵

label.en: Thăng Long taken, then retaken by Trần forces
label.zh: 升龙失守后被陈军收复

label.en: Yuan fleet destroyed at Bạch Đằng
label.zh: 元军舰队覆灭于白藤江

sources.title: Đại Việt sử ký toàn thư (Complete Annals of Đại Việt, 1479; 1697 ed.)
Yuanshi (History of Yuan, 1370), "Annan zhuan" and "Zhaowa zhuan"
Keith W. Taylor, A History of the Vietnamese (Cambridge University Press, 2013)
Wikipedia: Mongol invasions of Vietnam

summary.en: Repeating Ngô Quyền's tactic, Trần Hưng Đạo staked the Bạch Đằng River and trapped the withdrawing Yuan fleet under Omar at low tide, destroying it and ending the third Mongol invasion.
summary.zh: 陈兴道效仿吴权的战法，在白藤江中埋设木桩，趁退潮困住撤退中的元朝乌马儿舰队并将其歼灭，结束了元朝第三次入侵。

sources.title: Đại Việt sử ký toàn thư (Complete Annals of Đại Việt, 1479; 1697 ed.)
Yuanshi (History of Yuan, 1370), "Annan zhuan" and "Zhaowa zhuan"
Keith W. Taylor, A History of the Vietnamese (Cambridge University Press, 2013)
Wikipedia: Battle of Bạch Đằng (1288)

summary.en: Kublai Khan sent a fleet to punish King Kertanegara of Singhasari for mutilating his envoy. Raden Wijaya allied with the Yuan to defeat the usurper Jayakatwang, then turned on and expelled them, founding Majapahit.
summary.zh: 忽必烈派遣舰队惩罚曾黥面元使的新柯沙里国王格尔达纳卡拉。罗登·威查耶先与元军联手击败篡位者查耶卡旺，随后反戈驱逐元军，建立了满者伯夷。

sources.title: Yuanshi (History of Yuan, 1370), "Annan zhuan" and "Zhaowa zhuan"
Pararaton (Book of Kings, 15th–16th c.)
M. C. Ricklefs, A History of Modern Indonesia since c. 1200 (Palgrave, 4th ed. 2008)
Wikipedia: Mongol invasion of Java

summary.en: Lê Lợi raised a rebellion against Ming occupation at Lam Sơn in Thanh Hóa. After a decade of guerrilla war and the destruction of a Ming relief army at Chi Lăng in 1427, the Ming withdrew and Lê Lợi founded the Later Lê dynasty.
summary.zh: 黎利在清化蓝山起兵反抗明朝统治。经过十年游击战，并于1427年在支棱歼灭明朝援军后，明军撤离，黎利建立后黎朝。

sources.title: Đại Việt sử ký toàn thư (Complete Annals of Đại Việt, 1479; 1697 ed.)
Keith W. Taylor, A History of the Vietnamese (Cambridge University Press, 2013)
Wikipedia: Lam Sơn uprising

summary.en: An Ayutthayan army besieged and took the Khmer capital. The Khmer court soon moved south toward the Phnom Penh area, closing the Angkorian era.
summary.zh: 阿瑜陀耶军队围攻并攻陷高棉都城。高棉王廷随后南迁至金边一带，吴哥时代就此结束。

sources.title: David Chandler, A History of Cambodia (Westview, 4th ed. 2008)
Royal Chronicles of Ayutthaya, trans. Richard D. Cushman (Siam Society, 2000)
Wikipedia: Fall of Angkor

note: The 1431 date comes from later chronicles; historians see Angkor's decline as gradual and the date as conventional.

summary.en: The fugitive Palembang prince Parameswara settled at Malacca around 1400. With Ming recognition and its command of the strait, the port grew into the greatest entrepôt of Southeast Asia and a centre for the spread of Islam.
summary.zh: 流亡的巨港王子拜里米苏拉约在1400年定居马六甲。凭借明朝的册封和对海峡的控制，这座港口发展为东南亚最大的转口贸易中心，也是伊斯兰教传播的中心。

sources.title: Encyclopaedia Britannica: Sultanate of Malacca
Sejarah Melayu (Malay Annals), trans. C. C. Brown (1952)
Tomé Pires, Suma Oriental (1512–1515), trans. Armando Cortesão (Hakluyt Society, 1944)
Barbara Watson Andaya & Leonard Y. Andaya, A History of Malaysia (Palgrave, 3rd ed. 2017)
Wikipedia: Malacca Sultanate

note: Founding dates between c. 1396 and 1402 are proposed.

summary.en: Afonso de Albuquerque's fleet stormed Malacca after weeks of fighting, driving out Sultan Mahmud Shah. Portugal gained a key base on the spice route, while Muslim traders dispersed to rival ports such as Aceh, Johor and Banten.
summary.zh: 阿方索·德·阿尔布克尔克的舰队经数周激战攻占马六甲，苏丹马哈茂德沙出逃。葡萄牙由此获得香料航线上的关键据点，穆斯林商人则分散到亚齐、柔佛、万丹等竞争港口。

sources.title: Brás de Albuquerque, Commentaries of the Great Afonso Dalboquerque (1557; Hakluyt Society trans. 1875–84)
Tomé Pires, Suma Oriental (1512–1515), trans. Armando Cortesão (Hakluyt Society, 1944)
Barbara Watson Andaya & Leonard Y. Andaya, A History of Malaysia (Palgrave, 3rd ed. 2017)
Wikipedia: Capture of Malacca (1511)

summary.en: Ferdinand Magellan, seeking to force the chief Lapulapu to submit to his Christian ally Rajah Humabon of Cebu, landed on Mactan with about 50 men and was killed. The expedition sailed on and completed the first circumnavigation in 1522.
summary.zh: 麦哲伦为迫使酋长拉普拉普臣服于已受洗的宿务王胡马邦，率约五十人登陆麦克坦岛，结果战死。船队继续航行，并于1522年完成首次环球航行。

label.en: Exits the Strait of Magellan into the Pacific (Nov 1520)
label.zh: 驶出麦哲伦海峡进入太平洋（1520年11月）
利马萨瓦岛：首次弥撒（3月31日）

sources.title: Antonio Pigafetta, Relazione del primo viaggio intorno al mondo (c. 1524), trans. R. A. Skelton (1969)
Encyclopaedia Britannica: Ferdinand Magellan
Wikipedia: Battle of Mactan

note: QID Q2091449 is the correct item, but its English label on Wikidata is currently vandalised ("Battle of Six Seven"); this record does not use the Wikidata label, and the label should be reverted on Wikidata.

summary.en: After defeating Rajah Sulayman's Maynila, Miguel López de Legazpi proclaimed the Spanish city of Manila, later walled as Intramuros. It became the capital of the Spanish Philippines and the Asian terminus of the Manila galleons to Acapulco.
summary.zh: 米格尔·洛佩斯·德·黎牙实比击败苏莱曼王统治的马尼拉后，宣布建立西班牙马尼拉城，后筑城墙成为王城区（Intramuros）。这里成为西属菲律宾首府和通往阿卡普尔科的马尼拉大帆船贸易的亚洲终点。

sources.title: Encyclopaedia Britannica: Intramuros
Emma H. Blair & James A. Robertson (eds.), The Philippine Islands, 1493–1898, Vol. 3 (1903)
Nicholas Tarling (ed.), The Cambridge History of Southeast Asia, Vol. 1: From Early Times to c. 1800 (1992)
Wikipedia: Intramuros

summary.en: Jan Pieterszoon Coen of the Dutch East India Company (VOC) destroyed the town of Jayakarta and built Batavia on its ruins. It became the VOC's Asian headquarters and later the capital of the Dutch East Indies.
summary.zh: 荷兰东印度公司的扬·彼得松·库恩摧毁查雅加达城，并在废墟上兴建巴达维亚。这里成为荷兰东印度公司的亚洲总部，后来成为荷属东印度首府。

sources.title: M. C. Ricklefs, A History of Modern Indonesia since c. 1200 (Palgrave, 4th ed. 2008)
Nicholas Tarling (ed.), The Cambridge History of Southeast Asia, Vol. 1: From Early Times to c. 1800 (1992)
Wikipedia: Batavia, Dutch East Indies

name.en: Burmese–Siamese War and fall of Ayutthaya
name.zh: 缅暹战争与阿瑜陀耶陷落

summary.en: Konbaung Burma under Hsinbyushin invaded Siam on two fronts and, after a 14-month siege, sacked and burned Ayutthaya in April 1767, ending the 417-year-old kingdom. Taksin soon regrouped the Siamese at Thonburi.
summary.zh: 贡榜王朝孟驳王分两路入侵暹罗，经十四个月围城，于1767年4月攻陷并焚毁阿瑜陀耶，延续四百余年的王国就此灭亡。不久郑信在吞武里重整暹罗力量。

sources.title: Victor Lieberman, Strange Parallels: Southeast Asia in Global Context, c. 800–1830, Vol. 1 (Cambridge University Press, 2003)
Chris Baker & Pasuk Phongpaichit, A History of Thailand (Cambridge University Press, 2nd ed. 2009)
Hmannan Yazawin (Glass Palace Chronicle, 1832)
Wikipedia: Burmese–Siamese War (1765–1767)

summary.en: King Rama I, founder of the Chakri dynasty, moved the capital across the Chao Phraya from Thonburi to Rattanakosin Island, setting the city pillar on 21 April 1782 and building the Grand Palace.
summary.zh: 却克里王朝开国君主拉玛一世将都城从吞武里迁至湄南河对岸的拉达那哥欣岛，于1782年4月21日立城柱，并修建大皇宫。

sources.title: Chris Baker & Pasuk Phongpaichit, A History of Thailand (Cambridge University Press, 2nd ed. 2009)
David K. Wyatt, Thailand: A Short History (Yale University Press, 2nd ed. 2003)
Wikipedia: Rattanakosin Island

summary.en: Nguyễn Huệ of the Tây Sơn, newly proclaimed Emperor Quang Trung, made a lightning march north during Tết and routed the Qing army that had occupied Thăng Long to restore the Lê, ending Qing intervention.
summary.zh: 西山朝阮惠刚称帝号光中，便于春节期间率军急行北上，击溃为扶持黎朝而占据升龙的清军，结束了清朝的干预。

sources.title: Keith W. Taylor, A History of the Vietnamese (Cambridge University Press, 2013)
Đại Việt sử ký toàn thư (Complete Annals of Đại Việt, 1479; 1697 ed.)
Wikipedia: Battle of Ngọc Hồi-Đống Đa

note: Wikidata gives 1788 (the Vietnamese lunar year Mậu Thân); the decisive fighting took place on 28–30 January 1789.

summary.en: The largest volcanic eruption in recorded history devastated Sumbawa, killing tens of thousands directly and through famine. Its aerosols cooled the northern hemisphere, causing the "Year Without a Summer" of 1816.
summary.zh: 有记录以来规模最大的火山喷发摧毁了松巴哇岛，直接或因饥荒死亡者数以万计。喷发的气溶胶使北半球降温，导致1816年出现“无夏之年”。

sources.title: Clive Oppenheimer, "Climatic, environmental and human consequences of the largest known historic eruption: Tambora volcano (Indonesia) 1815", Progress in Physical Geography 27:2 (2003)
M. C. Ricklefs, A History of Modern Indonesia since c. 1200 (Palgrave, 4th ed. 2008)
Wikipedia: 1815 eruption of Mount Tambora

summary.en: Prince Diponegoro of Yogyakarta led a widespread rebellion against Dutch colonial rule and its Javanese allies. The war cost some 200,000 Javanese lives before Diponegoro was seized at negotiations and exiled.
summary.zh: 日惹王子蒂博尼哥罗领导了一场反抗荷兰殖民统治及其爪哇盟友的大规模起义。战争造成约二十万爪哇人死亡，最终蒂博尼哥罗在谈判中被扣押并流放。

sources.title: Encyclopaedia Britannica: Java War
Peter Carey, The Power of Prophecy: Prince Dipanagara and the End of an Old Order in Java, 1785–1855 (KITLV, 2007)
M. C. Ricklefs, A History of Modern Indonesia since c. 1200 (Palgrave, 4th ed. 2008)
Wikipedia: Java War

summary.en: A cataclysmic eruption destroyed most of Krakatoa island in the Sunda Strait. Tsunamis killed more than 36,000 people on Java and Sumatra, and the explosion was heard thousands of kilometres away.
summary.zh: 巽他海峡的喀拉喀托岛发生灾难性喷发，岛屿大部被摧毁。引发的海啸在爪哇和苏门答腊造成三万六千余人死亡，爆炸声远传数千公里。

sources.title: G. J. Symons (ed.), The Eruption of Krakatoa and Subsequent Phenomena (Royal Society, 1888)
M. C. Ricklefs, A History of Modern Indonesia since c. 1200 (Palgrave, 4th ed. 2008)
Wikipedia: 1883 eruption of Krakatoa

summary.en: The secret society Katipunan under Andrés Bonifacio launched an armed revolt against Spain in August 1896; the execution of José Rizal fuelled it. Led later by Emilio Aguinaldo, revolutionaries declared independence on 12 June 1898.
summary.zh: 1896年8月，安德烈斯·博尼法西奥领导的秘密组织卡蒂普南发动反抗西班牙的武装起义，黎刹遭处决更激化了革命。后在埃米利奥·阿吉纳尔多领导下，革命者于1898年6月12日宣布独立。

sources.title: Encyclopaedia Britannica: Philippine Revolution
Teodoro A. Agoncillo, The Revolt of the Masses: The Story of Bonifacio and the Katipunan (1956)
Nicholas Tarling (ed.), The Cambridge History of Southeast Asia, Vol. 2: The Nineteenth and Twentieth Centuries (1992)
Wikipedia: Philippine Revolution

summary.en: The People's Party, a group of military officers and civilian officials, staged a bloodless coup in Bangkok that ended absolute monarchy and gave Siam its first constitution under King Prajadhipok.
summary.zh: 由军官与文官组成的民党在曼谷发动不流血政变，结束了君主专制，在巴差提勃国王治下颁布暹罗第一部宪法。

sources.title: Encyclopaedia Britannica: Siamese revolution of 1932
Chris Baker & Pasuk Phongpaichit, A History of Thailand (Cambridge University Press, 2nd ed. 2009)
David K. Wyatt, Thailand: A Short History (Yale University Press, 2nd ed. 2003)
Wikipedia: Siamese revolution of 1932

summary.en: Two days after Japan's surrender, Sukarno and Mohammad Hatta read a brief proclamation of independence at Sukarno's house in Jakarta. Four years of war and diplomacy followed before the Netherlands transferred sovereignty in 1949.
summary.zh: 日本投降两天后，苏加诺与穆罕默德·哈达在雅加达苏加诺寓所宣读简短的独立宣言。此后经过四年的战争与外交斗争，荷兰才于1949年移交主权。

sources.title: M. C. Ricklefs, A History of Modern Indonesia since c. 1200 (Palgrave, 4th ed. 2008)
J. D. Legge, Sukarno: A Political Biography (Allen Lane, 1972)
Wikipedia: Proclamation of Indonesian Independence

summary.en: At Ba Đình Square in Hanoi, Hồ Chí Minh proclaimed the Democratic Republic of Vietnam after the August Revolution, quoting the US Declaration of Independence. France's return to Indochina led to war the following year.
summary.zh: 八月革命后，胡志明在河内巴亭广场宣布越南民主共和国成立，并引用了美国《独立宣言》的语句。法国重返印度支那，次年爆发战争。

sources.title: Hồ Chí Minh, Tuyên ngôn độc lập (Declaration of Independence), 2 September 1945
William J. Duiker, Ho Chi Minh: A Life (Hyperion, 2000)
Wikipedia: Declaration of independence of the Democratic Republic of Vietnam

summary.en: Việt Minh forces under Võ Nguyên Giáp hauled artillery onto the hills around a French fortified valley and forced its surrender after 56 days. The defeat ended French rule in Indochina at the Geneva Conference.
summary.zh: 武元甲指挥越盟军队将火炮运上环绕法军谷地要塞的山头，经五十六天围攻迫使守军投降。此役使法国在日内瓦会议上结束了对印度支那的统治。

sources.title: Encyclopaedia Britannica: Battle of Điện Biên Phủ
Bernard B. Fall, Hell in a Very Small Place: The Siege of Dien Bien Phu (Lippincott, 1966)
Fredrik Logevall, Embers of War: The Fall of an Empire and the Making of America's Vietnam (Random House, 2012)
Wikipedia: Battle of Dien Bien Phu

summary.en: A war between communist North Vietnam with the southern National Liberation Front and the US-backed South Vietnam. US troop strength passed 500,000 in 1968 and peaked at about 543,000 in 1969; after the US withdrawal of 1973, Saigon fell in April 1975 and Vietnam was reunified.
summary.zh: 以越南北方及南方民族解放阵线为一方、美国支持的南越为另一方的战争。美军在越兵力于1968年超过五十万，1969年达到约54.3万的峰值；1973年美军撤出后，西贡于1975年4月陷落，越南实现统一。

label.en: US Marines land at Đà Nẵng

summary.en: After Andrés de Urdaneta found the eastward return route across the Pacific in 1565, Spanish galleons sailed between Manila and Acapulco for 250 years, exchanging Chinese silk and porcelain for Mexican and Peruvian silver. The trade tied Asia to the Americas and made silver a global currency.

summary.en: After reawakening in April, Pinatubo on Luzon produced the second-largest eruption of the 20th century on 15 June 1991, as a typhoon passed. Forecasts by Philippine and US volcanologists allowed mass evacuations that saved thousands of lives; the sulphur cloud cooled the globe by about 0.5 °C.

summary.en: The gravestone of Malik al-Salih, first Muslim ruler of Samudera Pasai in northern Sumatra, is dated 696 AH (1297). Marco Polo, passing in 1292, found nearby Perlak already Muslim; Pasai became the first major Islamic sultanate of Southeast Asia, visited by Ibn Battuta in 1345.
summary.zh: 苏门答腊北部须文答剌-巴赛首位穆斯林统治者马利克·萨利赫的墓碑纪年为伊斯兰历696年（1297年）。1292年途经此地的马可·波罗记载附近的八儿剌（佩尔拉克）已信奉伊斯兰教；巴赛成为东南亚第一个重要的伊斯兰苏丹国，1345年伊本·白图泰曾到访。

summary.en: In a valley behind the Cham capital, King Bhadravarman dedicated a wooden shrine to Shiva around 400; for nine centuries Cham kings rebuilt it in brick and stone into some seventy temple towers. American bombing in 1969 destroyed many of them.
summary.zh: 约400年，占婆国王跋陀罗跋摩在都城后方的山谷中建起一座供奉湿婆的木构神殿；此后九个世纪，历代占婆国王以砖石重建扩建，形成约七十座塔庙。1969年美军轰炸摧毁了其中许多建筑。

summary.en: Isanavarman I made Isanapura (Sambor Prei Kuk) the capital of Chenla, raising octagonal brick temples decorated with "flying palaces". The Sui history describes a city of 20,000 households, the largest pre-Angkorian centre in Cambodia.
summary.zh: 伊奢那跋摩一世以伊奢那补罗（三波坡雷古）为真腊都城，修建饰有“飞宫”浮雕的八角形砖塔。《隋书》称其城有二万余家，是柬埔寨吴哥以前最大的中心。

summary.en: The Tang monk Yijing stopped at Srivijaya on his way to India in 671 to learn Sanskrit, and returned in 687 to spend years copying and translating scriptures. His Record of Buddhist Practices, written there, describes over a thousand monks at the Srivijayan court.
summary.zh: 唐代僧人义净于671年赴印度途中在室利佛逝停留学习梵语，687年又返回此地，多年抄写、翻译佛经。他在此写成的《南海寄归内法传》记载，室利佛逝王城有僧侣千余人。

sources.title: Yijing, Nanhai jigui neifa zhuan (A Record of Buddhist Practices Sent Home from the Southern Sea, 691)
O. W. Wolters, Early Indonesian Commerce (Cornell University Press, 1967)
Wikipedia: Yijing (monk)

story.en:
In the winter of 671 Yijing boarded a Persian merchant ship at Guangzhou. Twenty days later he landed at Foshi, Srivijaya, on the Musi river in Sumatra, and stayed six months to study Sanskrit grammar before the king sent him on, in a royal ship, to Malayu and India. He spent more than a decade at Nalanda.

On the way home he stopped again at Srivijaya, and found it the ideal place to work. He advised Chinese monks bound for India to train there first, because its teachers followed the same rules as in India. Running short of paper and ink, he went back to Guangzhou in 689 on a ship that sailed unexpectedly, recruited helpers and returned.

From Srivijaya he sent home his Record of Buddhist Practices and a book of biographies of pilgrim monks. Together they are our best picture of the 7th-century Malay world: a trading kingdom on the monsoon route whose rulers made it a centre of Buddhist learning, a role the Kedukan Bukit inscription of 683 also hints at.
story.zh:
671年冬，义净在广州登上一艘波斯商船，二十天后抵达苏门答腊穆西河畔的“佛逝”（室利佛逝），停留半年学习梵文文法，随后国王派船送他前往末罗瑜和印度。他在那烂陀寺学习了十余年。

归途中他再次来到室利佛逝，认为这里是译经的理想之地。他建议赴印度求法的中国僧人先在此修学，因为当地的师资和戒律与印度相同。689年他因缺少纸墨，搭上一艘意外起航的商船回到广州，招募助手后又返回室利佛逝。

他从室利佛逝寄回了《南海寄归内法传》和《大唐西域求法高僧传》。这两部书是了解7世纪马来世界最好的资料：一个位于季风航路上的贸易王国，其统治者使之成为佛学中心；683年的格杜干武吉碑铭也暗示了这一点。

name.zh: 珊阇耶王的康加尔碑铭

summary.en: A Sanskrit inscription on Mount Wukir in Central Java records King Sanjaya's dedication of a Shiva linga in 732. It is the earliest dated record of the Mataram kingdom, whose rulers would build Borobudur and Prambanan.
summary.zh: 中爪哇乌基尔山上的梵文碑铭，记载了732年珊阇耶王供奉湿婆林伽之事。这是马打兰王国最早有确切纪年的记录，该王国后来修建了婆罗浮屠和普兰巴南。

sources.title: George Cœdès, The Indianized States of Southeast Asia (University of Hawaii Press, 1968)
Paul Michel Munoz, Early Kingdoms of the Indonesian Archipelago and the Malay Peninsula (Editions Didier Millet, 2006)
Wikipedia: Canggal inscription

name.zh: 伊洛瓦底江的骠国城邦

summary.en: Beikthano, Halin and Sri Ksetra were walled brick cities with irrigated fields, Buddhist stupas and urn burials, the first urban civilisation of Burma. A Pyu embassy with musicians reached Chang'an in 802; a Nanzhao raid in 832 broke their power.
summary.zh: 毗湿奴城、汉林和室利差呾罗是筑有砖墙、灌溉农田、佛塔与瓮棺葬的城市，是缅甸最早的城市文明。802年骠国使团携乐工抵达长安；832年南诏的劫掠摧毁了骠国的势力。

sources.title: UNESCO World Heritage Centre: Pyu Ancient Cities
Xin Tangshu (New Book of Tang), "Treatise on the Piao"
Janice Stargardt, The Ancient Pyu of Burma (Cambridge, 1990)
Wikipedia: Pyu city-states

name.en: Jayavarman II consecrated on Phnom Kulen
name.zh: 阇耶跋摩二世在荔枝山受封

summary.en: On Mahendraparvata, the Kulen plateau north of Angkor, a Brahmin performed a rite making Jayavarman II a chakravartin, universal monarch, and freeing the Khmer from "Java". The ceremony, recorded 250 years later, is the conventional founding of the Khmer Empire.
summary.zh: 在吴哥以北的荔枝山（摩醯因陀罗山）上，一位婆罗门为阇耶跋摩二世举行仪式，奉其为“转轮王”，宣告高棉摆脱“爪哇”。这一由250年后的碑铭记载的仪式，被视为高棉帝国建立的传统标志。

sources.title: Sdok Kak Thom inscription (K. 235, 1052)
George Cœdès, The Indianized States of Southeast Asia (University of Hawaii Press, 1968)
David Chandler, A History of Cambodia (Westview, 4th ed. 2008)
Damian Evans et al., "Uncovering archaeological landscapes at Angkor using lidar", PNAS 110 (2013)
Wikipedia: Jayavarman II

note: The date 802 rests on the Sdok Kak Thom inscription; the QID is that of the mountain where the rite took place.

story.en:
Almost everything known about the founding of Angkor comes from one stone. In 1052 a family of court priests carved the Sdok Kak Thom inscription to record their own lineage, and in passing told how, two and a half centuries earlier, their ancestor had served a king named Jayavarman who "came from Java".

According to the inscription, Jayavarman spent years moving his court and subduing local lords across Cambodia. Then, on Mahendraparvata, "the mountain of the great Indra", a Brahmin named Hiranyadama performed a rite so that "Kambuja" would no longer depend on Java, and established the cult of the devaraja, the god-king, to be served by the priestly family forever. Historians still argue whether "Java" meant the island, a Malay power, or simply a foreign overlord.

The mountain city of Mahendraparvata itself was lost in the forest until 2012, when airborne lidar revealed a grid of streets, dykes and temples beneath the canopy of Phnom Kulen. Jayavarman later ruled from Hariharalaya, near Angkor, where his successors would build the greatest temple complex in the world.
story.zh:
关于吴哥建国的几乎所有信息都来自一块石碑。1052年，一个宫廷祭司家族刻下斯多卡通碑铭以记录本族世系，其中顺带讲述了两个半世纪前，他们的祖先如何侍奉一位“来自爪哇”的国王阇耶跋摩。

据碑铭记载，阇耶跋摩多年辗转迁移王廷，征服柬埔寨各地的首领。之后，在“大因陀罗之山”摩醯因陀罗山上，婆罗门希兰亚达摩举行仪式，使“甘菩遮”不再依附爪哇，并确立了“神王”崇拜，由这一祭司家族世代奉祀。“爪哇”究竟指爪哇岛、某个马来政权，还是泛指外来宗主，史学家至今争论不休。

摩醯因陀罗山城本身长期湮没于森林之中，直到2012年机载激光雷达在荔枝山的树冠下发现了街道、堤坝和神庙组成的网格。阇耶跋摩后来以吴哥附近的诃里诃罗洲为都，他的继承者们将在那里建起世界上最宏伟的神庙群。

summary.en: King Anawrahta of Pagan took the Mon city of Thaton, carrying its king Manuha, monks, artisans and Pali scriptures back to Pagan. The conquest is remembered as the moment Theravada Buddhism became the religion of the Burmese state.
summary.zh: 蒲甘国王阿奴律陀攻占孟人城市直通，把国王摩奴诃、僧侣、工匠和巴利文三藏带回蒲甘。这次征服被视为上座部佛教成为缅甸国教的开端。

sources.title: Hmannan Yazawin (Glass Palace Chronicle, 1829)
Michael Aung-Thwin, The Mists of Rāmañña: The Legend that was Lower Burma (University of Hawaii Press, 2005)
Victor Lieberman, Strange Parallels: Southeast Asia in Global Context, c. 800–1830, vol. 1 (Cambridge University Press, 2003)
Wikipedia: Anawrahta

note: 1057 is the chronicle date. Aung-Thwin argues that the Thaton conquest story is a later legend; the QID is the Thaton kingdom, which Wikidata ends in 1057.

story.en:
The Burmese chronicles tell the story as a conversion. A Mon monk from Thaton, Shin Arahan, came to Pagan and so impressed King Anawrahta that the king swept away the old Ari priests and asked Manuha, king of Thaton, for a copy of the Pali scriptures. Manuha refused, and in 1057 Anawrahta marched south and besieged the city.

According to the chronicle, he brought back Manuha and his family, thousands of monks and craftsmen, and the Tipitaka loaded on thirty-two white elephants. Manuha, held captive at Pagan, is said to have built the Manuha temple, whose cramped interior with its huge Buddha images is read as an expression of his confinement.

Modern historians are divided. Michael Aung-Thwin argues that the conquest of Thaton is a legend created centuries later, since no contemporary inscription mentions it. What is clear is that from Anawrahta's reign Pagan became a Theravada kingdom, writing Pali and Mon, and that its kings began the building that left more than two thousand temples on the plain of Bagan.
story.zh:
缅甸编年史把这段历史讲成一次皈依。直通的孟族僧人信阿罗汉来到蒲甘，令阿奴律陀王深为折服；国王废黜了原来的阿利僧，并向直通国王摩奴诃索要巴利文三藏。摩奴诃拒绝了，1057年阿奴律陀挥师南下围攻直通。

据编年史记载，他带回了摩奴诃及其家眷、数千名僧侣和工匠，以及用三十二头白象驮载的三藏经典。被囚于蒲甘的摩奴诃据说建造了摩奴诃寺，寺内空间逼仄而佛像巨大，被解读为他身陷囹圄的心境写照。

现代史学家对此意见分歧。昂杜因认为征服直通是数百年后编造的传说，因为同时代的碑铭对此只字未提。可以确定的是，从阿奴律陀统治时起，蒲甘成为上座部佛教王国，使用巴利文与孟文，历代国王开始兴建佛塔，最终在蒲甘平原上留下了两千多座寺塔。

name.en: Battle of the Như Nguyệt River

summary.en: Song China invaded Đại Việt in 1076–1077 in revenge for Lý Thường Kiệt's raids on Guangxi. Lý Thường Kiệt held the Như Nguyệt (Cầu) river line north of Thăng Long; disease and failed crossings forced the Song to accept peace and withdraw.
summary.zh: 为报复李常杰对广西的袭击，宋朝于1076—1077年入侵大越。李常杰在升龙以北据守如月江（梂江）防线；宋军渡河失败，又遭疫病，被迫议和撤军。

sources.title: Keith W. Taylor, A History of the Vietnamese (Cambridge University Press, 2013)
Songshi (History of Song), "Biography of Jiaozhi"
James Anderson, The Rebel Den of Nùng Trí Cao (University of Washington Press, 2007)
Wikipedia: Song–Đại Việt war

story.en:
In late 1075 Lý Thường Kiệt struck first. Hearing that the reformist Song minister Wang Anshi was preparing an invasion, he led an army and fleet into Guangxi, took Qinzhou and Lianzhou and, after a siege of forty-two days, sacked Yongzhou (Nanning) early in 1076, killing much of its population.

The Song counter-attack under Guo Kui reached the Như Nguyệt river, a day's march from Thăng Long, early in 1077. Lý Thường Kiệt had fortified the south bank with palisades. The Song could not get their fleet up the coast to support a crossing, and the attacks that did cross were thrown back. Disease swept the Song camp.

Vietnamese tradition says that one night a voice from the riverside temple recited the poem "Nam quốc sơn hà": the southern country belongs to the southern emperor, as fixed in the book of heaven, and invaders will meet defeat. Its authorship and date are debated, but it is often called Vietnam's first declaration of independence. Guo Kui accepted a truce and withdrew, keeping only a few border districts that were later returned.
story.zh:
1075年末，李常杰先发制人。他听说宋朝变法派宰相王安石正筹划入侵，便率水陆大军攻入广西，夺取钦州、廉州，1076年初又在围城四十二日后攻破邕州（南宁），城中居民死伤甚众。

1077年初，郭逵率宋军反攻，抵达距升龙仅一日路程的如月江。李常杰早已在南岸筑起栅寨。宋军舰队无法沿海北上配合渡江，渡过江的部队又被击退，军营中疫病流行。

越南传说某夜江边神祠中传出诗句：“南国山河南帝居，截然定分在天书，如何逆虏来侵犯，汝等行看取败虚。”这首《南国山河》的作者与年代仍有争议，但常被称为越南第一篇独立宣言。郭逵最终接受议和撤军，只保留了几处边境州县，后来也归还了大越。

summary.en: King Kyansittha's Ananda Temple, a cross-shaped shrine with four standing Buddhas and gilded spires, became the masterpiece of early Pagan architecture. Its corridors hold hundreds of glazed plaques and stone reliefs of the Buddha's lives.
summary.zh: 江喜陀王建造的阿难陀寺呈十字形，内有四尊立佛，塔顶镀金，是蒲甘早期建筑的杰作。寺内回廊镶嵌着数百块釉陶板和佛本生故事石雕。

sources.title: UNESCO World Heritage Centre: Bagan
G. H. Luce, Old Burma–Early Pagán (J. J. Augustin, 1969–70)
Wikipedia: Ananda Temple

note: Construction is dated c. 1090–1105; Wikidata gives 1091 as the start.

summary.en: A four-sided stone stele dated 1292, found at Sukhothai in 1833 by the future King Mongkut, praising King Ram Khamhaeng's benevolent rule and claiming that he devised the Thai script. Long a national icon, its authenticity has been debated since the 1980s.
summary.zh: 一块四面刻字的石碑，所署年代为1292年，1833年由后来的蒙固王在素可泰发现。碑文颂扬兰甘亨王的仁政，并称泰文字母由他创制。它长期被视为国宝，但自20世纪80年代起其真伪一直存在争议。

sources.title: A. B. Griswold & Prasert na Nagara, "The Inscription of King Rāma Gamhèn of Sukhodaya (1292 A.D.)", Journal of the Siam Society 59 (1971)
James R. Chamberlain (ed.), The Ram Khamhaeng Controversy (Siam Society, 1991)
UNESCO Memory of the World: The King Ram Khamhaeng Inscription (2003)
Wikipedia: Ram Khamhaeng Inscription

note: Most scholars accept it as 13th-century; Michael Vickery and Piriya Krairiksh argued it was composed in the 19th century.

story.en:
In 1833 the monk-prince Mongkut, on pilgrimage at the ruins of Sukhothai, noticed a stone pillar lying near an old throne. It was covered on four sides in an archaic script. Deciphered, it spoke in the voice of King Ram Khamhaeng: in his time "there are fish in the water and rice in the fields"; the king hung a bell at his palace gate so that any subject with a grievance could ring it; and in 1283 he had invented the Thai letters.

The pillar became the founding text of the Thai nation, taught to every schoolchild and inscribed in 2003 on UNESCO's Memory of the World register. But its very perfection raised doubts. In the 1980s the historian Michael Vickery and the art historian Piriya Krairiksh pointed to spelling, vocabulary and ideas that seemed closer to the 19th century, suggesting Mongkut himself might have composed it to show Siam's ancient civilisation to Western powers.

The debate has not been settled, though most epigraphers now accept a 13th-century date, perhaps with later additions. Either way, the stone shaped how Thais imagine their past.
story.zh:
1833年，出家为僧的王子蒙固在素可泰遗址朝圣时，发现一座古王座旁躺着一根石柱，四面刻满古老的文字。破译后，碑文以兰甘亨王的口吻说：在他统治时“水中有鱼，田里有稻”；国王在宫门挂了一口钟，任何有冤屈的臣民都可以敲响它；1283年他创制了泰文字母。

这根石柱成为泰国的立国文献，每个学童都要学习，2003年还列入联合国教科文组织《世界记忆名录》。但它的完美本身引起了怀疑。20世纪80年代，历史学家迈克尔·维克里和艺术史家披利雅·格莱力指出，碑文的拼写、词汇和思想似乎更接近19世纪，暗示可能是蒙固本人为向西方列强展示暹罗的古老文明而撰写的。

这场争论至今没有定论，不过多数碑铭学家现在接受13世纪的年代，或许其中有后人增补。无论如何，这块石碑塑造了泰国人对自身过去的想象。

summary.en: A member of a Yuan embassy, Zhou Daguan lived at Angkor for about a year and wrote "The Customs of Cambodia", the only eyewitness account of the city at its height: its golden towers, royal processions, markets run by women and Chinese settlers.
summary.zh: 元朝使团成员周达观在吴哥居住约一年，写成《真腊风土记》。这是唯一一部亲历吴哥鼎盛时期的记述，描写了金塔、王家仪仗、由妇女经营的集市和当地的华人移民。

sources.title: Zhou Daguan, Zhenla fengtu ji, trans. Peter Harris, A Record of Cambodia: The Land and Its People (Silkworm Books, 2007)
David Chandler, A History of Cambodia (Westview, 4th ed. 2008)
Wikipedia: The Customs of Cambodia

story.en:
In 1296 an embassy sent by Temür Khan, Kublai's successor, sailed from Wenzhou to Cambodia. Among its members was Zhou Daguan, a young man from Zhejiang, who stayed at Angkor from August 1296 to July 1297 and afterwards wrote a short book about what he saw.

He described the walled city of Angkor Thom with a golden tower at its centre (the Bayon), the king riding out on an elephant under white parasols with hundreds of palace women carrying candles, and the bridge lined with stone giants. He noted that trade was the business of women, so Chinese sailors who settled there were quick to take local wives; that slaves were taken from the hill peoples; and that the Cambodians bathed in groups in the rivers several times a day.

His account also hints at strain: the country had recently been devastated by war with the Siamese. Lost for centuries in Chinese collections, the book was translated into French in 1819 and guided the first European explorers of Angkor, and it remains the only description of the city written while it was still living.
story.zh:
1296年，忽必烈的继承者元成宗派遣使团从温州出海前往真腊。使团中有一位来自浙江的年轻人周达观，他于1296年8月至1297年7月留居吴哥，归国后写下一部小书，记录所见所闻。

他描写了城墙环绕的吴哥通王城，城中心有一座金塔（巴戎寺）；国王骑象出巡，张白伞盖，数百宫女手持蜡烛随行；城门石桥两侧排列着石刻巨神。他记载当地贸易由妇女经营，因此在此定居的中国水手很快就娶了当地妻子；奴隶多取自山地民族；当地人每天数次成群到河中洗浴。

他的记述也透露出危机：真腊不久前刚遭暹罗战火蹂躏。这部书在中国典籍中沉寂数百年，1819年被译成法文，引导了最早一批探访吴哥的欧洲人。它至今仍是唯一一部在吴哥尚有生机时写下的城市记录。

summary.en: Mangrai, having conquered Haripunchai and seen his earlier capital at Wiang Kum Kam flood, founded Chiang Mai, the "new city", between Doi Suthep and the Ping river. The chronicle says his allies Ngam Muang of Phayao and Ram Khamhaeng of Sukhothai helped lay it out.
summary.zh: 孟莱王征服哈里奔猜后，因原先的都城温孔岗遭水淹，便在素贴山与滨河之间兴建“新城”清迈。据编年史记载，帕尧的昂孟王和素可泰的兰甘亨王协助他规划了这座城市。

sources.title: David K. Wyatt & Aroonrut Wichienkeeo (trans.), The Chiang Mai Chronicle (Silkworm Books, 2nd ed. 1998)
Hans Penth, A Brief History of Lan Na (Silkworm Books, 1994)
Wikipedia: Chiang Mai

note: The founding date is from the Chiang Mai Chronicle; Wikidata gives a 13th-century inception.

name.zh: 加查·马达的帕拉帕誓言

summary.en: On becoming chief minister of Majapahit, Gajah Mada swore, according to the Pararaton, that he would taste no palapa (spice, or pleasure) until he had united the islands of the archipelago under Majapahit. Modern Indonesia adopted the oath as a symbol of national unity.
summary.zh: 据《诸王志》记载，加查·马达出任满者伯夷宰相时发誓：在把群岛诸岛统一于满者伯夷之前，绝不享用“帕拉帕”（香料，或享乐）。现代印尼把这一誓言当作民族统一的象征。

sources.title: Pararaton (Book of Kings), Old Javanese chronicle
Theodore G. Th. Pigeaud, Java in the 14th Century: A Study in Cultural History (Martinus Nijhoff, 1960–63)
M. C. Ricklefs, A History of Modern Indonesia since c. 1200 (4th ed., Stanford University Press, 2008)
Wikipedia: Palapa oath

note: Known only from the later Pararaton; the meaning of "palapa" is uncertain. Indonesia named its first communications satellite Palapa (1976).

summary.en: The Sundanese king came to Majapahit to marry his daughter Dyah Pitaloka to Hayam Wuruk. Gajah Mada demanded that she be handed over as a token of submission; the Sundanese royal party fought and was killed to a man at the Bubat field, and the princess is said to have taken her life.
summary.zh: 巽他国王带着女儿迪亚·毗塔洛卡前往满者伯夷与哈奄·武禄成婚。加查·马达要求把公主作为臣服的贡品献上，巽他王室随员奋起抵抗，在布巴特广场全数战死，据说公主也随之自尽。

sources.title: Pararaton (Book of Kings), Old Javanese chronicle
Kidung Sunda (Middle Javanese poem)
Theodore G. Th. Pigeaud, Java in the 14th Century: A Study in Cultural History (Martinus Nijhoff, 1960–63)
Wikipedia: Battle of Bubat

note: Known from the Pararaton and the Kidung Sunda, not from the Nagarakretagama; the event soured Javanese–Sundanese relations for centuries.

summary.en: Prince U Thong, ruler of a Tai-Chinese trading family, moved his court to an island in the Chao Phraya, perhaps fleeing epidemic, and was crowned Ramathibodi I. Ayutthaya soon absorbed Sukhothai, sacked Angkor and became the main power of mainland Southeast Asia.
summary.zh: 出身泰华贸易家族的乌通王子，或许为躲避瘟疫，将王廷迁到湄南河中的一座岛上，加冕为拉玛铁菩提一世。阿瑜陀耶很快吞并素可泰、攻陷吴哥，成为东南亚大陆的主要强国。

sources.title: Royal Chronicles of Ayutthaya (Luang Prasoet version)
Chris Baker & Pasuk Phongpaichit, A History of Ayutthaya (Cambridge University Press, 2017)
Wikipedia: Ayutthaya Kingdom

note: The date is from the Luang Prasoet chronicle; a settlement existed on the site earlier.

summary.en: Returning from exile at Angkor with a Khmer army, Fa Ngum subdued the Lao principalities of the middle Mekong and was crowned at Xieng Dong Xieng Thong (Luang Prabang), founding Lan Xang, the "million elephants" kingdom that is the ancestor of Laos.
summary.zh: 法昂率高棉军队从吴哥流亡归来，征服湄公河中游的老族诸邦，在川铜（琅勃拉邦）加冕，建立“百万大象”澜沧王国，即老挝的前身。

sources.title: Martin Stuart-Fox, The Lao Kingdom of Lān Xāng: Rise and Decline (White Lotus, 1998)
Nithan Khun Borom (Lao chronicle)
Wikipedia: Lan Xang

note: The date is traditional (some sources 1354); Wikidata's coordinate is a country centroid.

name.zh: 大越攻陷毗阇耶（阇槃城）

summary.en: Lê Thánh Tông led a vast army south and stormed Vijaya (Chà Bàn), the Cham capital near Quy Nhơn, killing and capturing tens of thousands and taking King Trà Toàn prisoner. Champa never recovered; its rump states survived further south until the 19th century.
summary.zh: 黎圣宗率大军南下，攻破归仁附近的占城都城毗阇耶（阇槃），杀死和俘获数万人，生擒国王槃罗茶全。占城从此一蹶不振，残余小邦在更南方苟延至19世纪。

sources.title: Keith W. Taylor, A History of the Vietnamese (Cambridge University Press, 2013)
Đại Việt sử ký toàn thư (Complete Annals of Đại Việt, 1479; 1697 ed.)
Ming shilu (Veritable Records of the Ming), Chenghua reign
Wikipedia: Đại Việt–Champa War (1471)

note: Casualty figures come from the Vietnamese annals and may be inflated; the QID is the Vijaya (Đồ Bàn) citadel site.

story.en:
By the 1460s Champa had fought Đại Việt on and off for five centuries, and in 1470 its king Trà Toàn attacked the Vietnamese frontier garrisons. Lê Thánh Tông answered with the largest army the country had ever raised: the annals speak of 260,000 men and a war fleet that sailed down the coast.

In March 1471 the Vietnamese reached Vijaya, the Cham capital on the plain behind Quy Nhơn. After a siege of a few days it fell. The annals record 40,000 killed and 30,000 captured, among them Trà Toàn and fifty members of the royal family; the king died on the voyage north. Lê Thánh Tông annexed the land as far as the Cù Mông pass and set up the province of Quảng Nam, and he divided the remaining Cham territory into small client states.

The Ming court, to which both kingdoms sent tribute, protested but did nothing. The fall of Vijaya ended Champa as a regional power and opened the long Vietnamese "march to the south" that reached the Mekong delta three centuries later.
story.zh:
到15世纪60年代，占城与大越断断续续交战已有五个世纪。1470年占城国王槃罗茶全进攻大越边防。黎圣宗以越南有史以来最庞大的军队回应：史书称有二十六万人，另有战船沿海南下。

1471年3月，大越军抵达归仁平原后方的占城都城毗阇耶，围城数日即破。据越南史书记载，杀四万人、俘三万人，其中包括槃罗茶全和五十名王族成员，国王在押往北方的途中死去。黎圣宗将直到瞿蒙关的土地并入版图，设广南道，又把剩下的占城领土分为几个附属小国。

两国都向明朝朝贡，明廷虽提出抗议却未采取行动。毗阇耶的陷落终结了占城作为地区强国的地位，开启了越南漫长的“南进”，三个世纪后一直推进到湄公河三角洲。

summary.en: During the fourth Burmese invasion of Ayutthaya, King Naresuan met the Burmese crown prince Mingyi Swa near Suphan Buri. Thai chronicles say Naresuan killed him in single combat on war elephants; the invasion collapsed and Siam stayed free of Burmese overlordship.
summary.zh: 缅甸第四次入侵阿瑜陀耶时，纳黎萱王在素攀武里附近与缅甸王储明吉斯瓦相遇。泰国编年史称纳黎萱在战象对决中将其斩杀；缅军入侵随即瓦解，暹罗从此摆脱缅甸的宗主权。

sources.title: Chris Baker & Pasuk Phongpaichit, A History of Thailand (Cambridge University Press, 2nd ed. 2009)
Chris Baker & Pasuk Phongpaichit, A History of Ayutthaya (Cambridge University Press, 2017)
Hmannan Yazawin (Glass Palace Chronicle, 1829)
Wikipedia: Battle of Nong Sarai

note: Thai and Burmese chronicles give different accounts of the duel and different dates (the Thai date 18 January 1593 is commemorated as Royal Thai Armed Forces Day).

name.en: Dutch conquest of the Banda Islands
name.zh: 荷兰征服班达群岛（班达大屠杀）

summary.en: To secure a monopoly of nutmeg and mace, Jan Pieterszoon Coen invaded the Banda Islands with VOC troops and Japanese mercenaries. Thousands of Bandanese were killed, starved or enslaved and deported; the islands were resettled with Dutch planters working imported slaves.
summary.zh: 为垄断肉豆蔻与肉豆蔻衣，燕·彼得逊·昆率荷兰东印度公司军队和日本雇佣兵入侵班达群岛。数千班达人被杀、饿死或沦为奴隶遭流放，群岛随后由荷兰种植园主带着输入的奴隶重新占据。

sources.title: Vincent C. Loth, "Armed Incidents and Unpaid Bills: Anglo-Dutch Rivalry in the Banda Islands", Modern Asian Studies 29 (1995)
Willard A. Hanna, Indonesian Banda: Colonialism and its Aftermath in the Nutmeg Islands (ISHI, 1978)
M. C. Ricklefs, A History of Modern Indonesia since c. 1200 (4th ed., Stanford University Press, 2008)
Wikipedia: Dutch conquest of the Banda Islands

note: The pre-conquest population (often put at about 15,000) and the numbers killed are estimates; the Dutch figures were 2,800 killed and 1,700 enslaved.

story.en:
In the early 17th century the Banda Islands, a speck of volcanic islands in the Banda Sea, were the only place on earth where nutmeg grew. Their elected elders, the orang kaya, sold to Javanese, Malay, English and Dutch buyers alike, and broke the exclusive contracts the Dutch pressed on them.

Jan Pieterszoon Coen, governor-general of the VOC, decided to end the problem by force. In early 1621 he landed on Lonthor with about two thousand men, including Japanese mercenaries. Villages were burned, and many Bandanese fled to the mountains, where they died of hunger, or jumped from cliffs rather than surrender. Accused of conspiracy, some forty orang kaya were tortured and then beheaded and quartered by the Japanese soldiers inside a bamboo enclosure; a Dutch officer who witnessed it recorded his horror.

Within a few years only a fraction of the population remained on the islands. Survivors were shipped to Batavia as slaves or escaped to the Kei islands, whose villages still speak Bandanese. The VOC divided the nutmeg groves into perken worked by slaves under Dutch perkeniers, a system that lasted two centuries. Even the Heeren XVII in Amsterdam rebuked Coen for his methods.
story.zh:
17世纪初，班达海中星点般的火山小岛班达群岛是世界上唯一出产肉豆蔻的地方。岛上推举的长老“奥朗卡亚”同时向爪哇、马来、英国和荷兰商人出售香料，屡次违背荷兰人强加的独家合约。

荷兰东印度公司总督燕·彼得逊·昆决定用武力解决问题。1621年初，他率约两千人（包括日本雇佣兵）登陆伦托尔岛。村庄被焚毁，许多班达人逃进山中饿死，或宁愿跳崖也不投降。约四十名奥朗卡亚被控谋反，遭受酷刑后在一个竹围栏内被日本兵斩首分尸；在场的一名荷兰军官记下了自己的惊恐。

几年之内，岛上只剩下原有人口的一小部分。幸存者被作为奴隶运往巴达维亚，或逃到凯伊群岛，那里的村庄至今仍讲班达语。公司把肉豆蔻林分成若干“园地”，由荷兰园主驱使奴隶耕作，这一制度延续了两个世纪。就连阿姆斯特丹的十七人董事会也谴责了昆的手段。

name.zh: 苏丹阿贡围攻巴达维亚

summary.en: Sultan Agung of Mataram twice sent armies across Java to drive the VOC from Batavia. Both sieges failed; in 1629 Dutch ships burned the rice stores Mataram had stockpiled at Tegal and Cirebon, and the besiegers starved. Coen died of disease inside the town.
summary.zh: 马打兰苏丹阿贡两次派大军横越爪哇，试图把荷兰东印度公司赶出巴达维亚，均告失败。1629年荷兰船只焚毁了马打兰囤积在直葛和井里汶的粮仓，围城军队陷入饥荒。昆在城中病逝。

label.zh: 第二次围攻巴达维亚失败

sources.title: M. C. Ricklefs, A History of Modern Indonesia since c. 1200 (4th ed., Stanford University Press, 2008)
H. J. de Graaf, De regering van Sultan Agung (Nijhoff, 1958)
Wikipedia: Siege of Batavia

note: Wikidata's coordinate lies in Central Java; the point here is Batavia itself.

story.en:
By the 1620s Sultan Agung ruled almost all of Java except two places: the old port of Banten and the Dutch fort at Batavia, which he regarded as an upstart vassal that refused to pay homage. In August 1628 his fleet and army appeared before the town. Mataram's troops dug trenches and tried to dam the river to flood the walls, but the Dutch held, and by December the attackers withdrew. Agung is said to have executed the commanders who failed him.

The second campaign, in 1629, was planned more carefully, with rice depots along the north coast to feed tens of thousands of soldiers. The VOC learned of them, and its ships sailed along the coast burning the barns at Tegal and Cirebon. When the Javanese army arrived, it was already hungry, and the siege collapsed in disease and starvation.

Inside Batavia, Coen died in September 1629, probably of dysentery. Agung never again attacked the Dutch, and their fort survived to become the capital of an empire that would eventually swallow Mataram itself.
story.zh:
到17世纪20年代，苏丹阿贡几乎统治了整个爪哇，只剩两处例外：老港万丹和荷兰人在巴达维亚的城堡。在他看来，后者是个拒不朝贡的暴发户藩属。1628年8月，他的舰队和大军兵临城下。马打兰军队挖掘壕沟，并试图筑坝引河水淹城墙，但荷兰人坚守不退，到12月进攻者撤兵。据说阿贡处死了作战不力的将领。

1629年的第二次远征准备更加周密，沿北海岸设立了粮站，以供给数万士兵。荷兰东印度公司得知后，派船沿海岸焚毁了直葛和井里汶的粮仓。爪哇军队抵达时已经饥肠辘辘，围城最终在疫病和饥饿中瓦解。

城内的昆于1629年9月去世，很可能死于痢疾。阿贡此后再未进攻荷兰人，而这座城堡存续下来，成为一个最终吞并马打兰本身的帝国的首都。

summary.en: A VOC fleet allied with the Sultanate of Johor besieged Portuguese Malacca for more than five months. Famine and disease killed most of the defenders and townspeople before the Dutch stormed the fortress on 14 January 1641, ending 130 years of Portuguese rule.
summary.zh: 荷兰东印度公司舰队与柔佛苏丹国联手围攻葡属马六甲五个多月。守军和居民大多死于饥荒和疫病，1641年1月14日荷兰人攻破要塞，结束了葡萄牙130年的统治。

sources.title: Barbara Watson Andaya & Leonard Y. Andaya, A History of Malaysia (Palgrave, 3rd ed. 2017)
C. R. Boxer, The Dutch Seaborne Empire 1600–1800 (Hutchinson, 1965)
Wikipedia: Siege of Malacca (1640–1641)

summary.en: Two clans ruling in the name of the powerless Lê emperors fought seven campaigns across the Gianh river: the Trịnh in the north (Đàng Ngoài) and the Nguyễn in the south (Đàng Trong). Nguyễn walls at Đồng Hới, built with Portuguese cannon, held; the truce of 1672 split Vietnam for a century.
summary.zh: 以傀儡黎帝名义执政的两大家族隔灵江七次交战：北方（塘外）的郑主与南方（塘中）的阮主。阮主在洞海修筑的长垒配备葡萄牙大炮，屡挡郑军；1672年停战后越南南北分治长达一个世纪。

sources.title: Keith W. Taylor, A History of the Vietnamese (Cambridge University Press, 2013)
Li Tana, Nguyễn Cochinchina: Southern Vietnam in the Seventeenth and Eighteenth Centuries (Cornell SEAP, 1998)
Wikipedia: Trịnh–Nguyễn War

summary.en: The VOC admiral Cornelis Speelman, allied with the Bugis prince Arung Palakka of Bone, attacked the Gowa sultanate, the great free port of eastern Indonesia. Sultan Hasanuddin signed the Treaty of Bongaya in 1667; when fighting resumed, the fortress of Somba Opu fell in June 1669.
summary.zh: 荷兰东印度公司将领斯皮尔曼与骨部的布吉斯王子阿隆·帕拉卡结盟，进攻印尼东部最大的自由港戈瓦苏丹国。哈桑努丁苏丹于1667年签订《本加亚条约》；战事再起后，松巴奥普要塞于1669年6月陷落。

sources.title: Leonard Y. Andaya, The Heritage of Arung Palakka (Martinus Nijhoff, 1981)
M. C. Ricklefs, A History of Modern Indonesia since c. 1200 (4th ed., Stanford University Press, 2008)
Wikipedia: Makassar War

name.zh: 红溪惨案（1740年巴达维亚大屠杀）

summary.en: Amid rumours of a Chinese uprising, VOC soldiers and townspeople killed some 10,000 ethnic Chinese in Batavia over two weeks in October 1740. The Chinese quarter burned, survivors joined Javanese rebels in a war that spread along the coast, and Governor-General Valckenier was recalled and imprisoned.
summary.zh: 在华人起事的谣言中，1740年10月荷兰东印度公司士兵和市民在两周内杀害了巴达维亚约一万名华人。华人区被焚，幸存者与爪哇起义者联合，战火沿海岸蔓延；总督瓦尔肯尼尔被召回并遭监禁。

sources.title: Leonard Blussé, Strange Company: Chinese Settlers, Mestizo Women and the Dutch in VOC Batavia (Foris, 1986)
M. C. Ricklefs, A History of Modern Indonesia since c. 1200 (4th ed., Stanford University Press, 2008)
Wikipedia: 1740 Batavia massacre

story.en:
Batavia depended on its Chinese: they milled its sugar, built its houses, collected its taxes and ran its shops. By the 1730s, however, the sugar trade had slumped, unemployed Chinese labourers filled the countryside, and the VOC began deporting "surplus" Chinese to Ceylon. A rumour spread that the deportees were being thrown overboard at sea.

In early October 1740 bands of Chinese attacked VOC posts outside the walls. Inside the city, Governor-General Adriaan Valckenier's council ordered a curfew and house searches. On 9 October fires broke out in the Chinese quarter, and soldiers, sailors and townspeople, among them many slaves, began to kill. Patients in the hospital and prisoners in the jail were murdered. Over the following days some 10,000 people died, and the Kali Angke canal is said to have run red, which is why Chinese call the event Hongxi, the "Red River".

Survivors fled east and joined forces with Javanese rebels in the "China War" that engulfed the north coast and led to the division of Mataram. In Amsterdam the directors recalled Valckenier, who died in prison in Batavia in 1751 before his trial ended.
story.zh:
巴达维亚离不开华人：他们经营糖厂、建造房屋、包收税款、开设店铺。然而到18世纪30年代，糖业衰退，失业的华人劳工遍布城郊，荷兰东印度公司开始把“多余”的华人遣送锡兰。随即有谣言说，被遣送者在海上被扔下船。

1740年10月初，成群的华人袭击了城外的公司哨所。城内，总督阿德里安·瓦尔肯尼尔的议会下令宵禁和搜查民宅。10月9日，华人区燃起大火，士兵、水手和市民（其中有许多奴隶）开始杀戮，医院里的病人和监狱中的囚犯也惨遭杀害。此后数日约有一万人罹难，据说安格克河被鲜血染红，华人因此称之为“红溪惨案”。

幸存者向东逃亡，与爪哇起义者联合，掀起席卷北海岸的“华人战争”，并导致马打兰的分裂。阿姆斯特丹的董事会召回了瓦尔肯尼尔，他在审判结束前于1751年死于巴达维亚的狱中。

summary.en: Three brothers from Tây Sơn village in Bình Định led a rebellion against the Nguyễn lords' taxes in 1771 that grew into a thirty-year civil war. They overthrew the Nguyễn, Trịnh and Lê, defeated Siamese and Qing armies, and were finally destroyed by the surviving Nguyễn prince, Nguyễn Ánh.
summary.zh: 1771年，平定西山邑的三兄弟因不堪阮主苛税而起事，演变为长达三十年的内战。他们先后推翻阮主、郑主和后黎朝，击败暹罗与清朝军队，最终被阮氏遗孤阮福映所灭。

label.en: Gia Định taken; Nguyễn lords killed
Siamese routed at Rạch Gầm–Xoài Mút
Nguyễn Ánh takes Phú Xuân and the north
label.zh: 阮福映攻取富春及北方

sources.title: Keith W. Taylor, A History of the Vietnamese (Cambridge University Press, 2013)
George Dutton, The Tây Sơn Uprising (University of Hawaii Press, 2006)
Wikipedia: Tây Sơn wars

name.en: Gia Long founds the Nguyễn dynasty

summary.en: Having defeated the Tây Sơn, Nguyễn Phúc Ánh proclaimed the Gia Long reign at Phú Xuân (Huế) and, for the first time, ruled a Vietnam stretching from the Chinese border to the Gulf of Thailand. In 1804 the Qing recognised the country as Việt Nam.
summary.zh: 击败西山朝后，阮福映在富春（顺化）改元嘉隆，首次统治北起中国边界、南至暹罗湾的完整越南。1804年清朝册封其国号为“越南”。

sources.title: Keith W. Taylor, A History of the Vietnamese (Cambridge University Press, 2013)
Alexander Woodside, Vietnam and the Chinese Model (Harvard University Press, 1971)
UNESCO World Heritage Centre: Complex of Huế Monuments
Wikipedia: Nguyễn dynasty

name.zh: 莱佛士建立英属新加坡

summary.en: Stamford Raffles and William Farquhar landed at the Singapore river in January 1819 and, by recognising Tengku Hussein as Sultan of Johor, won the right to set up an East India Company trading post. As a free port it grew within five years into the busiest entrepôt of the Straits.
summary.zh: 1819年1月，斯坦福·莱佛士和威廉·法夸尔在新加坡河口登陆，通过承认东姑胡先为柔佛苏丹，取得了设立东印度公司贸易站的权利。作为自由港，它在五年内成为马六甲海峡最繁忙的转口港。

sources.title: C. M. Turnbull, A History of Modern Singapore 1819–2005 (NUS Press, 2009)
John N. Miksic, Singapore and the Silk Road of the Sea, 1300–1800 (NUS Press, 2013)
Encyclopaedia Britannica: Singapore: History
Wikipedia: Founding of modern Singapore

story.en:
After the Napoleonic Wars Britain handed Java back to the Netherlands, and the Dutch moved to close the Straits of Malacca to British ships. Stamford Raffles, then lieutenant-governor of Bencoolen in Sumatra, persuaded the governor-general in Calcutta to let him find a new station at the southern end of the Straits.

On 28 January 1819 his ships anchored off the mouth of the Singapore river, where a few hundred Malays and Orang Laut lived under the Temenggong of Johor. Johor's throne was disputed, and the Dutch backed the younger brother. Raffles brought the elder, Tengku Hussein, over from the Riau islands, recognised him as sultan, and on 6 February signed a treaty with him and the Temenggong allowing the Company to build a factory in return for annual payments.

Raffles stayed only a few days, leaving William Farquhar in charge. He declared the port free of duties, and Chinese, Bugis, Arab and Indian traders poured in. The Dutch protested, but the Anglo-Dutch Treaty of 1824 left Singapore in British hands.
story.zh:
拿破仑战争结束后，英国把爪哇归还荷兰，荷兰随即试图对英国船只封锁马六甲海峡。时任苏门答腊明古鲁副总督的斯坦福·莱佛士说服加尔各答的总督，准许他在海峡南端另觅据点。

1819年1月28日，他的船队停泊在新加坡河口，那里有数百名马来人和海人，受柔佛天猛公管辖。柔佛王位当时存在争议，荷兰支持弟弟一方。莱佛士从廖内群岛接来哥哥东姑胡先，承认他为苏丹，并于2月6日与他和天猛公签约：公司可在此建立商馆，作为回报每年付给二人款项。

莱佛士只停留了几天，便把事务交给威廉·法夸尔。他宣布新加坡为免税的自由港，华人、布吉斯人、阿拉伯人和印度商人蜂拥而至。荷兰提出抗议，但1824年的《英荷条约》确认新加坡归英国所有。

summary.en: Border clashes over Arakan, Manipur and Assam led British India to invade Burma by sea. After Rangoon fell, disease killed far more British troops than battle, but General Bandula was killed at Danubyu and the Treaty of Yandabo (1826) cost Burma its western provinces and a huge indemnity.
summary.zh: 因阿拉干、曼尼普尔和阿萨姆的边境冲突，英属印度从海路入侵缅甸。仰光陷落后，英军死于疾病者远多于战死者，但缅军名将班都拉在达努彪阵亡，1826年的《杨达波条约》使缅甸失去西部诸省并支付巨额赔款。

sources.title: Thant Myint-U, The River of Lost Footsteps: Histories of Burma (Farrar, Straus and Giroux, 2006)
G. E. Harvey, History of Burma (Longmans, 1925)
Wikipedia: First Anglo-Burmese War

summary.en: Signed in London, the treaty divided the Malay world along the Straits of Malacca: Britain gave up Bencoolen in Sumatra, the Netherlands gave up Malacca and its objections to Singapore. The line it drew became, in effect, the border between Malaysia and Indonesia.
summary.zh: 该条约在伦敦签订，沿马六甲海峡瓜分马来世界：英国放弃苏门答腊的明古鲁，荷兰放弃马六甲并不再反对英国占有新加坡。条约划出的界线实际上成为后来马来西亚与印度尼西亚的边界。

sources.title: Barbara Watson Andaya & Leonard Y. Andaya, A History of Malaysia (Palgrave, 3rd ed. 2017)
Nicholas Tarling, Anglo-Dutch Rivalry in the Malay World, 1780–1824 (Cambridge University Press, 1962)
Wikipedia: Anglo-Dutch Treaty of 1824

note: Signed in London; the point marks the Strait of Malacca, where its line was drawn.

summary.en: Governor-General Van den Bosch required Javanese villages to grow export crops, above all coffee, sugar and indigo, on a share of their land or to work for the government. The profits rescued the Dutch treasury, while forced cropping contributed to famines in Cirebon and Central Java in the 1840s.
summary.zh: 总督范登博斯规定爪哇村庄须拿出部分土地种植咖啡、甘蔗、靛蓝等出口作物，或为政府服劳役。所得利润挽救了荷兰国库，而强迫种植则加剧了19世纪40年代井里汶和中爪哇的饥荒。

sources.title: M. C. Ricklefs, A History of Modern Indonesia since c. 1200 (4th ed., Stanford University Press, 2008)
Robert E. Elson, Village Java under the Cultivation System, 1830–1870 (Allen & Unwin, 1994)
Encyclopaedia Britannica: Culture System
Wikipedia: Cultivation System

note: Point placed in Central Java; the system covered most of Java.

summary.en: King Mongkut signed a treaty with Britain's envoy John Bowring fixing import duties at 3 per cent, ending royal trade monopolies and granting British subjects extraterritoriality. It opened Siam to free trade and rice exports, and similar treaties with other powers followed.
summary.zh: 蒙固王与英国使节约翰·宝宁签订条约，将进口关税定为3%，取消王室贸易专营，并给予英国臣民治外法权。条约使暹罗向自由贸易和大米出口开放，其他列强随后订立了类似条约。

sources.title: Chris Baker & Pasuk Phongpaichit, A History of Thailand (Cambridge University Press, 2nd ed. 2009)
John Bowring, The Kingdom and People of Siam (London, 1857)
Wikipedia: Bowring Treaty

summary.en: Over eight years the naturalist Alfred Russel Wallace collected some 125,000 specimens across the archipelago. On Ternate in 1858 he wrote the essay on natural selection that prompted Darwin to publish, and he noticed the sharp faunal boundary between Bali and Lombok now called the Wallace Line.
summary.zh: 博物学家阿尔弗雷德·拉塞尔·华莱士用八年时间在马来群岛采集了约十二万五千件标本。1858年他在特尔纳特写下关于自然选择的论文，促使达尔文发表其理论；他还注意到巴厘岛与龙目岛之间动物分布的明显界线，即今天所称的“华莱士线”。

sources.title: Alfred Russel Wallace, The Malay Archipelago (Macmillan, 1869)
Natural History Museum, London: Alfred Russel Wallace
Wikipedia: Wallace Line

note: Point placed on the Lombok Strait, where the line runs.

name.en: Siege of Tourane: French conquest begins
name.zh: 土伦之围：法国征服越南的开端

summary.en: Citing the persecution of Catholic missionaries, a Franco-Spanish fleet under Admiral Rigault de Genouilly seized Tourane (Đà Nẵng) in September 1858. Disease pinned the force down, so it turned south and took Saigon in 1859; by the treaty of 1862 Emperor Tự Đức ceded three provinces of Cochinchina.
summary.zh: 以天主教传教士遭迫害为由，里戈·德·热努伊率领的法西联合舰队于1858年9月攻占土伦（岘港）。疫病使远征军困守不前，于是转而南下，1859年攻占西贡；根据1862年条约，嗣德帝割让交趾支那东部三省。

sources.title: Pierre Brocheux & Daniel Hémery, Indochina: An Ambiguous Colonization, 1858–1954 (University of California Press, 2009)
Keith W. Taylor, A History of the Vietnamese (Cambridge University Press, 2013)
Wikipedia: Siege of Tourane

name.zh: 穆尔塔图里出版《马格斯·哈弗拉尔》

summary.en: Eduard Douwes Dekker, a former colonial official in Lebak, published under the pen name Multatuli a novel exposing the extortion of Javanese peasants by native chiefs and the Dutch authorities. It shocked Dutch readers and fed the campaign against the Cultivation System.
summary.zh: 曾在勒巴克任殖民官员的爱德华·道韦斯·德克尔以“穆尔塔图里”为笔名出版小说，揭露当地头人和荷兰当局对爪哇农民的盘剥。小说震动了荷兰读者，推动了反对强迫种植制度的运动。

sources.title: M. C. Ricklefs, A History of Modern Indonesia since c. 1200 (4th ed., Stanford University Press, 2008)
Encyclopaedia Britannica: Max Havelaar
Wikipedia: Max Havelaar

note: Point placed at Rangkasbitung, Lebak, where the story is set.

summary.en: The Netherlands invaded the Aceh Sultanate to stop it courting foreign powers. After the first expedition's commander was killed, a long guerrilla war led by ulama and nobles such as Teuku Umar and Cut Nyak Dhien followed; General van Heutsz's mobile columns broke organised resistance by 1904.
summary.zh: 荷兰为阻止亚齐苏丹国结交外国势力而发动入侵。首次远征的司令阵亡后，乌理玛和贵族（如特乌库·乌马尔和朱·娘·典）领导了旷日持久的游击战；范赫茨将军的机动纵队到1904年瓦解了有组织的抵抗。

sources.title: Anthony Reid, The Contest for North Sumatra (Oxford University Press, 1969)
M. C. Ricklefs, A History of Modern Indonesia since c. 1200 (4th ed., Stanford University Press, 2008)
Encyclopaedia Britannica: Aceh War
Wikipedia: Aceh War

note: Point at Kutaraja (Banda Aceh), where the war began; Wikidata's point is in central Aceh.

story.en:
In April 1873 a Dutch expedition landed near Kutaraja, the Acehnese capital, expecting a quick campaign. Within days its commander, General Köhler, was shot dead near the great mosque, and the troops withdrew. A second, larger force took the sultan's palace in 1874, and the Dutch declared the war won.

It had barely begun. The ulama preached holy war, and resistance passed from the court to village leaders. Teuku Umar famously changed sides in 1893, took Dutch arms and money and then deserted with them in 1896. His wife Cut Nyak Dhien fought on after his death, leading a dwindling band through the forests until she was betrayed in 1905.

The Dutch Islam scholar Christiaan Snouck Hurgronje, who had studied in Mecca, advised separating the uleebalang nobility from the ulama and crushing the latter. General J. B. van Heutsz put this into practice with small, mobile marechaussee units, and by 1904 the war was officially over, though killings continued for years. Tens of thousands of Acehnese and some 37,000 colonial soldiers and labourers died.
story.zh:
1873年4月，荷兰远征军在亚齐首都哥打拉惹附近登陆，本以为能速战速决。没过几天，司令克勒将军就在大清真寺附近中弹身亡，部队随即撤退。1874年，第二支规模更大的部队攻占了苏丹王宫，荷兰人宣布战争胜利。

其实战争才刚刚开始。乌理玛号召圣战，抵抗的重心从宫廷转向乡村首领。特乌库·乌马尔于1893年倒向荷兰，拿到武器和钱财后，1896年又带着它们倒戈而去，此事广为人知。他死后，妻子朱·娘·典继续作战，率领日渐稀少的部众在森林中辗转，直到1905年被人出卖。

曾在麦加求学的荷兰伊斯兰学者斯努克·许尔赫罗涅建议把贵族阶层与乌理玛分化开来，集中打击后者。范赫茨将军以小规模机动的宪兵队付诸实施，到1904年战争正式结束，但杀戮又持续了多年。数万名亚齐人以及约三万七千名殖民军士兵和劳工在战争中死去。

name.en: Third Anglo-Burmese War and the fall of Mandalay
name.zh: 第三次英缅战争与曼德勒陷落

summary.en: Using a timber company's dispute and fears of French influence as pretexts, British steamers carried an army up the Irrawaddy and took Mandalay within three weeks. King Thibaw and Queen Supayalat were exiled to Ratnagiri in India, and Upper Burma was annexed on 1 January 1886.
summary.zh: 英国以一家木材公司的纠纷和担心法国势力渗透为借口，用汽船沿伊洛瓦底江运兵北上，三周内攻占曼德勒。锡袍王和素帕雅叻王后被流放到印度拉特纳吉里，上缅甸于1886年1月1日被吞并。

sources.title: Thant Myint-U, The River of Lost Footsteps: Histories of Burma (Farrar, Straus and Giroux, 2006)
Thant Myint-U, The Making of Modern Burma (Cambridge University Press, 2001)
Wikipedia: Third Anglo-Burmese War

note: Mandalay fell on 28 November 1885; guerrilla resistance lasted into the 1890s.

summary.en: France joined Cochinchina, Annam, Tonkin and Cambodia into the Indochinese Union under one governor-general; Laos was added in 1893. The federation lasted until the defeat at Điện Biên Phủ.
summary.zh: 法国将交趾支那、安南、东京和柬埔寨合并为印度支那联邦，由一名总督统辖；1893年加入老挝。这一联邦一直维持到奠边府战败。

sources.title: Pierre Brocheux & Daniel Hémery, Indochina: An Ambiguous Colonization, 1858–1954 (University of California Press, 2009)
Encyclopaedia Britannica: French Indochina

summary.en: The Dutch army doctor Eugène Dubois, searching for a "missing link", dug up a skullcap and later a thigh bone on the Solo river at Trinil. He named the species Pithecanthropus erectus; now classed as Homo erectus, it was the first early human fossil found outside Europe.

summary.en: After buying the Philippines from Spain, the United States fought the First Philippine Republic. Aguinaldo's army turned to guerrilla war; US forces used reconcentration and the "water cure". Some 4,200 Americans and 20,000 Filipino soldiers died, and perhaps 200,000 or more civilians, mostly from disease and famine.

story.en:
By the Treaty of Paris of December 1898 Spain sold the Philippines to the United States for 20 million dollars. Filipinos who had proclaimed their own republic at Malolos refused to be transferred. On the night of 4 February 1899 an American sentry fired on Filipino soldiers near the San Juan bridge in Manila, and the war began.

In open battle the Filipino army was no match for the Americans, and by late 1899 Aguinaldo had dispersed it into guerrilla bands. The war turned brutal. After guerrillas killed 48 American soldiers at Balangiga, Samar, in September 1901, General Jacob Smith ordered the island turned into a "howling wilderness" and told his men to kill everyone over ten. In Batangas whole populations were herded into reconcentration zones where cholera and hunger killed thousands.

Aguinaldo was captured in March 1901 by Frederick Funston, whose men posed as prisoners of Macabebe scouts, and he called on Filipinos to accept American rule. President Theodore Roosevelt declared the war over on 4 July 1902. In the United States the war split opinion: Mark Twain and the Anti-Imperialist League denounced it, and Senate hearings exposed the use of torture.
story.zh:
根据1898年12月的《巴黎条约》，西班牙以两千万美元把菲律宾卖给美国。已在马洛洛斯宣布成立共和国的菲律宾人拒绝被转手。1899年2月4日夜，一名美国哨兵在马尼拉圣胡安桥附近向菲律宾士兵开枪，战争由此爆发。

在正面作战中，菲律宾军队远非美军对手，到1899年底阿奎纳多把部队化整为零，转入游击战。战争随之变得残酷。1901年9月，游击队在萨马岛巴兰吉加杀死48名美军士兵，雅各布·史密斯将军下令把全岛变成“哀号的荒野”，要部下杀死所有十岁以上的人。在八打雁，整村居民被驱入集中区，数以千计的人死于霍乱和饥饿。

1901年3月，弗雷德里克·芬斯顿让部下假扮马卡贝贝侦察兵押送的俘虏，俘获了阿奎纳多；阿奎纳多随后呼吁菲律宾人接受美国统治。1902年7月4日，西奥多·罗斯福总统宣布战争结束。这场战争在美国国内引发分裂：马克·吐温和反帝国主义联盟予以谴责，参议院听证会也揭露了酷刑的使用。
